messages.content: You are a research writing assistant. Cite via tools; do not invent sources.
Draft two sentences on how activation plateaus relate to error correction, with one real citation pointer.

I'll search for activation plateau literature first.
<tool_call>
{"name": "web_search", "arguments": {"query": "activation plateaus directional sensitivity LLMs Heimersheim Mendel"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
1. Heimersheim & Mendel 2024 — Activation plateaus and directional sensitivity in LLMs
</tool_response>

Fetching a short abstract snippet for accurate wording.
<tool_call>
{"name": "fetch_url", "arguments": {"url": "https://example.org/heimersheim-mendel-2024"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
Real activations sit in plateaus; small perturbations are suppressed more than expected.
</tool_response>

Activation plateaus suggest networks implement error correction: small residual-stream perturbations are suppressed rather than amplified. Heimersheim and Mendel (2024) link this geometry to directional sensitivity in LLMs.
You help edit longform writing via an outline store.
For doc essay42, tighten the intro thesis to one sentence and save it.

Loading the current intro section.
<tool_call>
{"name": "outline_store_get", "arguments": {"doc_id": "essay42", "section": "intro"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
This essay will discuss several ways cities change how people meet each other in parks and transit hubs over time.
</tool_response>

Condensing to a single thesis and saving.
<tool_call>
{"name": "outline_store_put", "arguments": {"doc_id": "essay42", "section": "intro", "text": "Cities reshape everyday social contact by redesigning the semi-public spaces where strangers routinely meet."}}
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
saved
</tool_response>
Saved thesis: cities reshape everyday social contact by redesigning the semi-public spaces where strangers routinely meet.

{"name": "style_guide_lookup", "arguments": {"rule": "avoid_utilize_empower"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
Prefer plain verbs: use, help. Avoid marketing cliches.
</tool_response>

Grabbing a calm on-brand example for cadence.
<tool_call>
{"name": "corpus_example", "arguments": {"tone": "plain_direct"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
We use simple methods that help people finish the task.
</tool_response>
Suggested rewrite: We use clear methods that help people get work done.

<tool_response>
Mind the GAP 2026 — models may refuse in text while complying via tools.
</tool_response>

Drafting and counting.
